blocks.en: Unit 5 · Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph
blocks.es_reference: Unidad 5 · Isaac, Jacob y José

blocks.en: 1. Sarah's Death and the Cave of Machpelah
blocks.es_reference: 1. La Muerte de Sara y la Cueva de Macpela

blocks.en: Sarah died at 127 years of age in Hebron. Abraham, the man to whom God had promised the entire land of Canaan, owned not a single square foot of it. So he negotiated with the Hittites and purchased the cave of Machpelah for four hundred shekels of silver — the first piece of the promised land actually held in his hand. It was a burial plot. The down payment on a promise still unfulfilled. Abraham, Sarah, Isaac, Rebekah, Jacob, and Leah would all eventually be buried there. The grave became Israel's first deed of ownership. Faith holds promises so firmly that it buys burial ground in a land it has not yet inherited.
blocks.es_reference: Sara murió a los 127 años en Hebrón. Abraham, el hombre a quien Dios había prometido toda la tierra de Canaán, no poseía ni un solo metro cuadrado de ella. Así que negoció con los hititas y compró la cueva de Macpela por cuatrocientos siclos de plata — el primer pedazo de la tierra prometida realmente tenido en su mano. Era un sepulcro. El pago inicial de una promesa aún incumplida. Abraham, Sara, Isaac, Rebeca, Jacob y Lea serían todos eventualmente sepultados allí. La tumba se convirtió en la primera escritura de propiedad de Israel. La fe sostiene las promesas con tanta firmeza que compra terreno funerario en una tierra que aún no ha heredado.

blocks.en: 2. Rebekah at the Well
blocks.es_reference: 2. Rebeca en el Pozo

blocks.en: Abraham, now old, charged his chief servant Eliezer to find a wife for Isaac — not from the Canaanites, but from Abraham's own people in Mesopotamia. Eliezer set out with ten camels loaded with gifts. At the well outside Nahor's city, he prayed a remarkable prayer: "Let it be that the young woman to whom I say, 'Please let down your pitcher that I may drink,' and she says, 'Drink, and I will also give your camels a drink' — let her be the one You have appointed." Before he finished praying, Rebekah arrived, drew water, and offered it not only to Eliezer but to all his thirsty camels — an enormous physical labor. Eliezer worshiped God on the spot. Rebekah agreed to leave her family and go with him. When Isaac met her in the field at evening, he loved her, and she comforted him after his mother's death. God's guidance is rarely loud, but it is always specific to those who ask.
blocks.es_reference: Abraham, ya anciano, encargó a su siervo principal Eliezer encontrar una esposa para Isaac — no de los cananeos, sino del propio pueblo de Abraham en Mesopotamia. Eliezer partió con diez camellos cargados de regalos. En el pozo a las afueras de la ciudad de Nacor, oró una oración notable: "Que sea que la doncella a quien diga: 'Por favor, baja tu cántaro para que yo beba', y ella diga: 'Bebe, y también daré de beber a tus camellos' — sea ella la que Tú has designado". Antes de terminar de orar, llegó Rebeca, sacó agua y la ofreció no solo a Eliezer sino a todos sus camellos sedientos — un esfuerzo físico enorme. Eliezer adoró a Dios en el lugar. Rebeca aceptó dejar a su familia e ir con él. Cuando Isaac la encontró en el campo al atardecer, la amó, y ella lo consoló tras la muerte de su madre. La guía de Dios rara vez es ruidosa, pero siempre es específica para los que preguntan.

blocks.en: Genesis 24:27 (NKJV): "And he said, 'Blessed be the Lord God of my master Abraham, who has not forsaken His mercy and His truth toward my master. As for me, being on the way, the Lord led me to the house of my master's brethren.'"
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 24:27 (RVG): "Y dijo: Bendito sea Jehová, Dios de mi señor Abraham, que no apartó de mi señor su misericordia y su verdad; en cuanto a mí, estando en el camino, Jehová me guió a la casa de los hermanos de mi señor."

blocks.en: 3. Isaac, Esau, and Jacob: The Birthright Despised
blocks.es_reference: 3. Isaac, Esaú y Jacob: La Primogenitura Despreciada

blocks.en: Rebekah was barren for twenty years. Isaac prayed, and she conceived twins — Esau and Jacob. Even in the womb they struggled. God told Rebekah, "Two nations are in your womb... the older shall serve the younger." Esau came first, red and hairy. Jacob came second, gripping his brother's heel — his name means "supplanter" or "heel-grabber." Esau grew into a skillful hunter and his father's favorite. Jacob was a quiet man dwelling in tents, his mother's favorite. One day Esau came in famished from the field. Jacob was cooking lentil stew. "Feed me, please," Esau demanded. Jacob saw his moment: "Sell me your birthright as of this day." Esau replied, "I am about to die; so what is this birthright to me?" He sold his birthright for a bowl of stew. Hebrews 12 calls him a "profane person" for despising what was eternal in favor of what was temporary.
blocks.es_reference: Rebeca fue estéril durante veinte años. Isaac oró, y ella concibió gemelos — Esaú y Jacob. Aun en el vientre lucharon. Dios le dijo a Rebeca: "Dos naciones hay en tu vientre... el mayor servirá al menor". Esaú vino primero, rojo y velludo. Jacob vino segundo, agarrando el calcañar de su hermano — su nombre significa "suplantador" o "el que agarra el talón". Esaú creció como diestro cazador y favorito de su padre. Jacob era un hombre tranquilo que habitaba en tiendas, favorito de su madre. Un día Esaú llegó del campo desfallecido. Jacob estaba cocinando guiso de lentejas. "Te ruego me des a comer", exigió Esaú. Jacob vio su momento: "Véndeme en este día tu primogenitura". Esaú respondió: "He aquí yo me voy a morir; ¿para qué, pues, me servirá la primogenitura?" Vendió su primogenitura por un plato de guiso. Hebreos 12 lo llama "profano" por despreciar lo eterno a favor de lo temporal.

blocks.en: 4. The Stolen Blessing
blocks.es_reference: 4. La Bendición Robada

blocks.en: When Isaac was old and blind, he asked Esau to hunt game and prepare a meal so he could give him the patriarchal blessing. Rebekah overheard and devised a deception. She cooked goat to taste like venison, dressed Jacob in Esau's clothes, and covered his arms with goat hair to mimic Esau's hairiness. Jacob went in. Isaac was suspicious — "The voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau" — but proceeded with the blessing. When Esau returned and the deception was uncovered, Isaac trembled violently and Esau cried out with a bitter cry. The blessing could not be retracted. Jacob — the deceiver — received the blessing, but at terrible cost. He had to flee for his life. He would not see his parents again for over twenty years. The consequences of getting something the right way by the wrong means follow you for decades.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Isaac era viejo y ciego, le pidió a Esaú que cazara y preparara una comida para darle la bendición patriarcal. Rebeca oyó y tramó un engaño. Cocinó cabrito para que supiera a venado, vistió a Jacob con la ropa de Esaú y le cubrió los brazos con piel de cabra para imitar el vello de Esaú. Jacob entró. Isaac sospechó — "La voz es la voz de Jacob, pero las manos, las manos de Esaú son" — pero procedió con la bendición. Cuando Esaú regresó y se descubrió el engaño, Isaac tembló violentamente y Esaú clamó con clamor amargo. La bendición no podía retractarse. Jacob — el engañador — recibió la bendición, pero a un costo terrible. Tuvo que huir por su vida. No volvería a ver a sus padres durante más de veinte años. Las consecuencias de obtener algo correcto por medios equivocados te siguen durante décadas.

blocks.en: 5. Jacob's Ladder at Bethel
blocks.es_reference: 5. La Escalera de Jacob en Betel

blocks.en: Fleeing toward his uncle Laban in Haran, Jacob came to a certain place and lay down to sleep with a stone for his pillow. That night he dreamed: a ladder set up on the earth with its top reaching to heaven, angels of God ascending and descending on it. At the top stood the Lord, who repeated the Abrahamic covenant to Jacob: "I am with you and will keep you wherever you go... I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you." Jacob awoke in terror: "Surely the Lord is in this place, and I did not know it. How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven." He named the place Bethel — "house of God." Jesus would later say to Nathanael: "You shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man" (John 1:51). Christ is the ladder. The way between earth and heaven runs through Him.
blocks.es_reference: Huyendo hacia su tío Labán en Harán, Jacob llegó a cierto lugar y se acostó a dormir con una piedra por almohada. Esa noche soñó: una escalera puesta en la tierra con su cima llegando al cielo, ángeles de Dios subiendo y bajando por ella. En la cima estaba Jehová, quien repitió a Jacob el pacto abrahámico: "He aquí, yo estoy contigo, y te guardaré por dondequiera que fueres... no te dejaré hasta que haya hecho lo que te he dicho". Jacob despertó con temor: "Ciertamente Jehová está en este lugar, y yo no lo sabía. ¡Cuán terrible es este lugar! No es otra cosa que casa de Dios, y puerta del cielo". Llamó al lugar Betel — "casa de Dios". Jesús más tarde le diría a Natanael: "Veréis el cielo abierto, y a los ángeles de Dios que suben y descienden sobre el Hijo del Hombre" (Juan 1:51). Cristo es la escalera. El camino entre la tierra y el cielo pasa por Él.

blocks.en: 6. Laban: Twenty Years of Discipline
blocks.es_reference: 6. Labán: Veinte Años de Disciplina

blocks.en: Jacob came to Laban's house and fell in love with Rachel, his uncle's younger daughter. He agreed to work seven years for her hand. The years "seemed but a few days to him because of the love he had for her." But on the wedding night, Laban substituted the older sister, Leah. Jacob — the deceiver who had impersonated his older brother — was now deceived by an older sister impersonating a younger. The text is dripping with irony. Jacob worked another seven years for Rachel, then six more for his flocks. Twenty years total under a manipulative father-in-law. Through it all, God multiplied Jacob's livestock supernaturally. He had eleven sons in Laban's house — Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, and Joseph. When God finally said, "Return to the land of your fathers," Jacob fled with his family and herds. Laban pursued but God warned him in a dream not to harm Jacob. They parted with a covenant of separation.
blocks.es_reference: Jacob llegó a la casa de Labán y se enamoró de Raquel, la hija menor de su tío. Acordó trabajar siete años por su mano. Los años "le parecieron como pocos días, porque la amaba". Pero en la noche de bodas, Labán sustituyó a la hermana mayor, Lea. Jacob — el engañador que había suplantado a su hermano mayor — fue ahora engañado por una hermana mayor suplantando a la menor. El texto rezuma ironía. Jacob trabajó otros siete años por Raquel, luego seis más por sus rebaños. Veinte años en total bajo un suegro manipulador. A través de todo, Dios multiplicó el ganado de Jacob sobrenaturalmente. Tuvo once hijos en la casa de Labán — Rubén, Simeón, Leví, Judá, Dan, Neftalí, Gad, Aser, Isacar, Zabulón y José. Cuando Dios finalmente dijo: "Vuelve a la tierra de tus padres", Jacob huyó con su familia y rebaños. Labán lo persiguió, pero Dios le advirtió en un sueño que no hiciera daño a Jacob. Se separaron con un pacto de separación.

blocks.en: Pastoral Note: God does not abandon His chosen but He does discipline them. The twenty years under Laban were not God's absence from Jacob — they were God's hand on him, breaking the deceiver of his deceit. We sometimes meet our worst traits in the mirror of someone else's behavior. Sanctification is rarely gentle.
blocks.es_reference: Nota Pastoral: Dios no abandona a Sus escogidos, pero sí los disciplina. Los veinte años bajo Labán no fueron la ausencia de Dios — fueron Su mano sobre Jacob, quebrantando al engañador de su engaño. A veces vemos nuestros peores rasgos en el espejo del comportamiento de otro. La santificación rara vez es gentil.

blocks.en: 7. Wrestling at Peniel
blocks.es_reference: 7. Luchando en Peniel

blocks.en: As Jacob approached the land of Canaan, he learned that Esau was coming to meet him with four hundred men. Terrified, Jacob divided his camp, sent gifts ahead, and spent the night alone at the Jabbok River. There a Man wrestled with him until dawn. When the Man saw He could not prevail by ordinary means, He touched Jacob's hip and dislocated it. Still Jacob clung: "I will not let You go unless You bless me." The Man asked, "What is your name?" Jacob said, "Jacob" — meaning supplanter, deceiver. Then the Man said, "Your name shall no longer be Jacob, but Israel, for you have struggled with God and with men, and have prevailed." Jacob called the place Peniel — "the face of God" — saying, "I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved." The sun rose. He limped for the rest of his life. The strong man must be broken before he can be useful. God renames us when He has remade us.
blocks.es_reference: Cuando Jacob se acercaba a la tierra de Canaán, supo que Esaú venía a su encuentro con cuatrocientos hombres. Aterrorizado, Jacob dividió su campamento, envió regalos por delante y pasó la noche solo en el río Jaboc. Allí un Hombre luchó con él hasta el amanecer. Cuando el Hombre vio que no podía prevalecer por medios ordinarios, tocó la cadera de Jacob y se la descoyuntó. Aun así, Jacob se aferró: "No te dejaré, si no me bendices". El Hombre preguntó: "¿Cuál es tu nombre?" Jacob dijo: "Jacob" — que significa suplantador, engañador. Entonces el Hombre dijo: "No se dirá más tu nombre Jacob, sino Israel; porque has luchado con Dios y con los hombres, y has vencido". Jacob llamó al lugar Peniel — "el rostro de Dios" — diciendo: "Vi a Dios cara a cara, y fue librada mi alma". Salió el sol. Cojeó por el resto de su vida. El hombre fuerte debe ser quebrantado antes de ser útil. Dios nos cambia el nombre cuando nos ha rehecho.

blocks.en: 8. Joseph's Dreams and Betrayal
blocks.es_reference: 8. Los Sueños de José y la Traición

blocks.en: Joseph was the eleventh son of Jacob and the firstborn of Rachel. Jacob loved him more than all his brothers and gave him a tunic of many colors — a mark of favored status. Joseph was seventeen when he dreamed two dreams: in the first, his brothers' sheaves bowed to his; in the second, the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowed to him. He told his brothers. They hated him all the more. One day, sent to check on his brothers in the fields, Joseph found them at Dothan. They saw him coming. "Look, this dreamer is coming!" They stripped him, threw him into a pit, and sold him to passing Ishmaelite traders for twenty shekels of silver — bound for Egypt. They dipped his coat in goat's blood and showed it to Jacob, who tore his clothes and mourned for many days, refusing to be comforted. The favored son was gone. Or so it seemed.
blocks.es_reference: José era el undécimo hijo de Jacob y el primogénito de Raquel. Jacob lo amaba más que a todos sus hermanos y le dio una túnica de muchos colores — una marca de estatus favorecido. José tenía diecisiete años cuando soñó dos sueños: en el primero, las gavillas de sus hermanos se inclinaron ante la suya; en el segundo, el sol, la luna y once estrellas se inclinaron ante él. Se lo contó a sus hermanos. Lo aborrecieron aún más. Un día, enviado a ver a sus hermanos en los campos, José los encontró en Dotán. Lo vieron venir. "He aquí viene el soñador". Lo despojaron, lo arrojaron a un pozo y lo vendieron a unos mercaderes ismaelitas que pasaban por veinte siclos de plata — rumbo a Egipto. Mojaron su túnica en sangre de cabra y se la mostraron a Jacob, quien rasgó sus vestidos y lloró por muchos días, rehusando ser consolado. El hijo favorito se había ido. O eso parecía.

blocks.en: 9. Joseph in Egypt: Tested and Faithful
blocks.es_reference: 9. José en Egipto: Probado y Fiel

blocks.en: Joseph was sold to Potiphar, captain of Pharaoh's guard. "The Lord was with Joseph, and he was a successful man." Potiphar made him overseer of his entire house. Then Potiphar's wife began propositioning him daily. Joseph refused: "How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?" When she finally grabbed him, he fled, leaving his garment in her hand. She accused him falsely, and Potiphar threw him into prison. But "the Lord was with Joseph and showed him mercy." The keeper of the prison put everything under Joseph's hand. In prison, Joseph interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's chief butler and chief baker. The butler was restored as Joseph had said — but forgot Joseph for two full years. Faithfulness without recognition is the deepest test of character. Joseph passed it. He was thirty years old when he finally left that prison — thirteen years after being sold into slavery.
blocks.es_reference: José fue vendido a Potifar, capitán de la guardia de Faraón. "Jehová estaba con José, y fue varón próspero". Potifar lo puso como mayordomo de toda su casa. Entonces la mujer de Potifar comenzó a tentarlo diariamente. José se negó: "¿Cómo, pues, haría yo este grande mal, y pecaría contra Dios?" Cuando ella finalmente lo agarró, él huyó, dejando su manto en sus manos. Ella lo acusó falsamente, y Potifar lo arrojó a la cárcel. Pero "Jehová estaba con José y le extendió Su misericordia". El jefe de la cárcel puso todo bajo la mano de José. En la cárcel, José interpretó los sueños del jefe de los coperos y del jefe de los panaderos de Faraón. El copero fue restaurado como José había dicho — pero olvidó a José por dos años completos. La fidelidad sin reconocimiento es la prueba más profunda del carácter. José la pasó. Tenía treinta años cuando finalmente salió de esa cárcel — trece años después de ser vendido como esclavo.

blocks.en: 10. Joseph Exalted: From Prison to Palace
blocks.es_reference: 10. José Exaltado: De la Cárcel al Palacio

blocks.en: Pharaoh dreamed of seven fat cows devoured by seven gaunt cows, and seven plump ears of grain consumed by seven blighted ears. No magician in Egypt could interpret. Then the butler finally remembered Joseph. Brought from the dungeon, Joseph said immediately, "It is not in me; God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace." Seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine. Joseph also offered the wisdom no one had asked for: appoint a wise administrator to store grain during the plenty. Pharaoh said, "Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?" He put his signet ring on Joseph's finger, dressed him in fine linen, and made him second in all Egypt. Joseph was thirty. He had spent thirteen years of obscurity preparing for one moment of public service. God's preparation is always longer than the deployment. He took his Egyptian name (Zaphenath-paneah) and an Egyptian wife (Asenath), and bore two sons — Manasseh ("God has made me forget") and Ephraim ("God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction").
blocks.es_reference: Faraón soñó con siete vacas gordas devoradas por siete vacas flacas, y siete espigas llenas consumidas por siete espigas marchitas. Ningún mago en Egipto pudo interpretar. Entonces el copero finalmente recordó a José. Traído del calabozo, José dijo de inmediato: "No está en mí; Dios será el que dé respuesta propicia a Faraón". Siete años de abundancia seguidos de siete años de hambre. José también ofreció la sabiduría que nadie le había pedido: nombrar un administrador sabio para almacenar grano durante la abundancia. Faraón dijo: "¿Acaso hallaremos otro hombre como éste, en quien esté el Espíritu de Dios?" Puso su anillo de sellar en el dedo de José, lo vistió de lino fino y lo hizo segundo en todo Egipto. José tenía treinta años. Había pasado trece años de oscuridad preparándose para un momento de servicio público. La preparación de Dios siempre es más larga que el despliegue. Tomó su nombre egipcio (Zafnat-panea) y una esposa egipcia (Asenat), y tuvo dos hijos — Manasés ("Dios me hizo olvidar") y Efraín ("Dios me hizo fructificar en la tierra de mi aflicción").

blocks.en: 11. "Ye Thought Evil Against Me, But God Meant It for Good"
blocks.es_reference: 11. "Vosotros Pensasteis Mal Contra Mí, Mas Dios lo Encaminó a Bien"

blocks.en: The famine came as Joseph predicted. Jacob's sons traveled to Egypt to buy grain and stood before Joseph without recognizing him. After two visits and elaborate testing — the silver in the sacks, the demand for Benjamin, the planted cup — Joseph could contain himself no longer. He sent the Egyptians out and wept loudly. "I am Joseph your brother, whom you sold into Egypt. But now, do not be grieved or angry with yourselves... for God sent me before you to preserve life." Jacob — Israel — came down to Egypt with all his household, seventy souls in total. Pharaoh welcomed them in Goshen. Genesis ends with two deathbed scenes. Jacob blessed Joseph's sons, crossing his hands to put the younger ahead of the older — the pattern of Genesis. Then Jacob blessed his twelve sons, prophesying over each. Of Judah he said, "The scepter shall not depart from Judah... until Shiloh comes" — pointing forward to Christ. Joseph lived to see his great-grandchildren and died at 110. His final words: "God will surely visit you, and bring you out of this land to the land of which He swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob." He had his bones carried out of Egypt 400 years later by Moses. Faith reaches across centuries. And Genesis closes — its last word is "Egypt." A nation in a coffin, with a promise on its lips.
blocks.es_reference: El hambre llegó como José había predicho. Los hijos de Jacob viajaron a Egipto a comprar grano y estuvieron ante José sin reconocerlo. Después de dos visitas y pruebas elaboradas — la plata en los sacos, la exigencia de Benjamín, la copa plantada — José no pudo contenerse más. Despidió a los egipcios y lloró fuertemente. "Yo soy José vuestro hermano, el que vendisteis para Egipto. Ahora, pues, no os entristezcáis... porque para preservación de vida me envió Dios delante de vosotros". Jacob — Israel — descendió a Egipto con toda su casa, setenta almas en total. Faraón los recibió en Gosén. Génesis termina con dos escenas de lecho de muerte. Jacob bendijo a los hijos de José, cruzando sus manos para poner al menor por delante del mayor — el patrón de Génesis. Luego Jacob bendijo a sus doce hijos, profetizando sobre cada uno. De Judá dijo: "No será quitado el cetro de Judá... hasta que venga Siloh" — apuntando hacia Cristo. José vivió para ver a sus bisnietos y murió a los 110. Sus últimas palabras: "Dios ciertamente os visitará, y os hará subir de esta tierra a la tierra que juró a Abraham, a Isaac y a Jacob". Hizo que sus huesos fueran sacados de Egipto 400 años después por Moisés. La fe alcanza a través de los siglos. Y Génesis cierra — su última palabra es "Egipto". Una nación en un ataúd, con una promesa en los labios.

blocks.en: Genesis 50:20 (NKJV): "But as for you, you meant evil against me; but God meant it for good, in order to bring it about as it is this day, to save many people alive."
blocks.es_reference: Génesis 50:20 (RVG): "Vosotros pensasteis mal contra mí, mas Dios lo encaminó a bien, para hacer lo que vemos hoy, para mantener en vida a mucho pueblo."

Πεντάτευχος

mc.stem: Where did Abraham purchase the cave of Machpelah, and what was its significance?
options: In Hebron, as a burial plot and the first piece of the promised land he owned
In Egypt, as a tax shelter
In Ur, as a family memorial
In Haran, as a trading post
mc.why: Correct. Abraham bought the cave in Hebron for 400 shekels — the first deed in the promised land, a down payment on a promise still unfulfilled.

mc.stem: What was Eliezer's task when Abraham sent him on a journey?
options: To find a wife for Isaac from Abraham's relatives
mc.why: Yes. Abraham insisted Isaac's wife not come from the Canaanites but from his own people in Mesopotamia.

mc.stem: What was the sign Eliezer asked God to give him at the well?
options: A young woman would offer water to him and his camels
A young woman would speak Hebrew
A young woman would wear a veil
A young woman would refuse him
mc.why: Correct. The sign required enormous physical labor — watering ten thirsty camels — and revealed Rebekah's character.

mc.stem: What did God tell Rebekah about her twin sons before they were born?
options: The older would serve the younger
mc.why: Yes. Two nations were in her womb, and the older (Esau) would serve the younger (Jacob).

mc.stem: What did Esau sell to Jacob, and for what?
options: His birthright, for a bowl of lentil stew
mc.why: Correct. Esau despised what was eternal in favor of what was temporary — Hebrews 12 calls him a 'profane person.'

mc.stem: How did Jacob obtain Isaac's blessing intended for Esau?
options: By bringing better food than Esau
By disguising himself in Esau's clothes and goat hair
mc.why: Yes. Rebekah dressed Jacob in Esau's clothes and covered his arms with goat hair to deceive blind Isaac.

mc.stem: What did Jacob see in his dream at Bethel?
options: A ladder reaching to heaven with angels ascending and descending
mc.why: Correct. The ladder pictured Christ — Jesus later told Nathanael He IS the ladder (John 1:51).

mc.stem: What did Jacob name the place of his dream?
mc.why: Yes. Bethel — 'house of God.' Jacob said, 'How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God.'

mc.stem: How many years did Jacob end up serving Laban total?
mc.why: Correct. Seven for Leah, seven more for Rachel, and six for his flocks — twenty years total of discipline under a manipulator.

mc.stem: What deception did Laban work on Jacob on his wedding night?
options: He substituted Leah, the older sister, for Rachel
mc.why: Yes. The deceiver was deceived — an older sister impersonating a younger, just as Jacob had impersonated his older brother.

mc.stem: What happened to Jacob when he wrestled with God at Peniel?
options: His hip was dislocated and his name was changed to Israel
mc.why: Correct. The strong man must be broken before he is useful. Jacob limped the rest of his life — and was renamed Israel.

mc.stem: What does the name 'Israel' mean?
options: 'One who struggles with God and prevails'
mc.why: Yes. The man said, 'You have struggled with God and with men, and have prevailed.'

mc.stem: Why did Joseph's brothers hate him?
options: Their father's favoritism, his colored tunic, and his prophetic dreams
mc.why: Correct. Favoritism plus dreams of dominion bred deep resentment — they couldn't even speak peaceably to him.

mc.stem: For how much did Joseph's brothers sell him to the Ishmaelite traders?
mc.why: Yes. Twenty shekels — pointing forward to Christ, who was also sold for silver by one of His own.

mc.stem: Why did Joseph end up in prison in Egypt?
options: Potiphar's wife falsely accused him after he refused her advances
mc.why: Correct. Joseph fled from her, leaving his garment behind — and she used that garment as false evidence.

mc.stem: How long did Joseph wait in prison after interpreting the butler's dream?
mc.why: Yes. The butler forgot Joseph for two years — faithfulness without recognition is the deepest test of character.

mc.stem: How old was Joseph when he was elevated to second in command of Egypt?
mc.why: Correct. Thirty years old — thirteen years of obscurity preparing for one moment of public service.

mc.stem: What was the meaning of Joseph's son Manasseh?
mc.why: Yes. 'God has made me forget all my toil and all my father's house' — gracious naming after years of pain.

mc.stem: What words did Joseph speak to his brothers when he revealed himself?
options: 'I am Joseph your brother whom you sold... but God sent me before you to preserve life'
'You will die for what you did'
mc.why: Correct. Joseph's theology of providence — God turned their evil into the saving of many lives (Genesis 50:20).

mc.stem: What were Joseph's final words to his brothers before he died?
options: 'God will surely visit you and bring you out of this land'
mc.why: Yes. Joseph's bones were carried out by Moses 400 years later — faith that reaches across centuries.

sa.prompt: What was the significance of Abraham purchasing the cave of Machpelah for Sarah's burial?
sa.model: Abraham owned no land in Canaan despite God's promise. The burial cave became Israel's first deed — a faith-based down payment on a promise still unfulfilled.

sa.prompt: Describe Eliezer's prayer at the well and what it teaches about seeking God's guidance.
sa.model: Eliezer asked for a sign that would reveal the woman's character (offering water to camels = enormous labor). God answered specifically before he finished praying — guidance is specific to those who ask.

sa.prompt: Why does Hebrews 12 call Esau a 'profane person' for selling his birthright?
sa.model: Esau despised the eternal blessing for momentary appetite. Trading what is eternal for what is temporary is the essence of profanity — treating sacred things as common.

sa.prompt: What is the significance of Jacob's ladder, and how does Christ fulfill that picture?
sa.model: The ladder connected earth to heaven, with angels traveling on it. Jesus told Nathanael He IS that ladder — the only way between God and humanity (John 1:51).

sa.prompt: How did God use Laban's twenty years of deception to discipline Jacob?
sa.model: Jacob the deceiver was deceived by an older sister substituting for a younger — mirroring his own deceit of his older brother. God broke the deceiver of his deceit.

sa.prompt: What does the wrestling match at Peniel teach about how God transforms His servants?
sa.model: God touched Jacob's hip to break him before blessing him. The strong man must be broken before he is useful. Jacob limped for life and was renamed Israel.

sa.prompt: How did Joseph respond to Potiphar's wife, and what does this reveal about his character?
sa.model: Joseph fled, leaving his garment. His refusal was framed not as 'sin against Potiphar' but 'sin against God' — his deepest accountability was upward, not horizontal.

sa.prompt: What is the significance of Joseph waiting two more years in prison after interpreting the butler's dream?
sa.model: Faithfulness without recognition is the deepest test of character. Joseph was forgotten for two years — God was forging in him the leader Egypt would need.

sa.prompt: Explain Joseph's statement: 'You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good' (Genesis 50:20).
sa.model: God's sovereign providence transforms human evil into His good purposes without excusing the evil. The same human action carries dual intent — and God's outweighs the human's. Foundation for Romans 8:28.

sa.prompt: What did Joseph's final words about being buried in the promised land teach about faith?
sa.model: Joseph trusted God's promise so completely that he made the next generation swear to carry his bones home. Moses carried them out 400 years later. Faith reaches across centuries.
